title: Saturday, October 31
script:
Good morning. Today is Saturday, October 31, 2026. Local time is five forty-one a.m.

Starting with the weather in Arkadelphia, today brings cloudy skies with a high near seventy-one degrees and an east southeast wind at zero miles per hour. There is a forty percent chance of rain showers after ten in the morning, with new rainfall amounts expected to stay under a tenth of an inch. Tonight brings a fifty percent chance of showers and thunderstorms before lowering slightly later, with a low around fifty-five degrees that will rise to around fifty-nine overnight. There are no active weather alerts. Sunrise will be at seven thirty-one a.m., and sunset at six nineteen p.m.

Turning to top headlines around the world, oil companies are reporting another quarter of sky-high profits, per NPR, as the ongoing war in Iran pushes up the price of oil and drives up costs at the pump. BBC News reports that the United States has approved the sale of five hundred Patriot missiles to Ukraine, providing American-made interceptors that remain crucial for downing Russian ballistic missiles. In the front-line town of Oleshky, BBC News notes that hundreds of people have been evacuated from the Russian-occupied area during a rare ceasefire, though many residents chose to stay despite the dangers. NPR also reports that a federal judge is opening a formal inquiry into potential Department of Justice misconduct in the Trump golf course case, investigating whether officials misled the court about their plans for the East Potomac municipal golf facility. In economic developments, a century-old paper mill in Témiscaming, Quebec, has indefinitely closed after the US imposed fifty percent tariffs on its products, putting hundreds of local residents out of work per BBC News.

In professional football, the Kansas City Chiefs hit the road to take on the Denver Broncos this Sunday afternoon in a high-stakes AFC West matchup. The Chiefs enter the game at five and one overall, looking to bounce back following a tough team-wide loss to the Seattle Seahawks last week. Head coach Andy Reid confirmed that cornerback Mansoor Delane is listed as questionable for Sunday after suddenly missing practice on Thursday and Friday with a recurring shoulder injury that has lingered since training camp. In roster moves reported by NFL.com, the Chiefs have signed veteran kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad. Across the league, the Denver Broncos prepare to host the rematch holding a five and two record, while analysts and former players continue to weigh in on Patrick Mahomes and the team's offensive adjustments ahead of kickoff.

Turning to Kansas men's basketball, the team is entering the final stretch of preseason preparations following its recent exhibition games. Preseason power rankings have dropped to highlight the top Jayhawks players heading into the campaign, while deep dives into the roster's depth continue under Bill Self.

For fantasy football managers sorting through lineups in Week 8, injury reports require close attention as players like Breece Hall and A.J. Brown navigate final game-day designations, while owners hunt for quarterback and tight end streamers. The waiver wire features key bench stashes and short-term fixes as the fantasy season reaches its midpoint.

Shifting to the weather in Los Angeles, today brings steady rain and cloudy skies with a high near sixty-eight degrees and a south southwest wind around five miles per hour. Rain will continue through the night with a low around fifty-nine degrees and a ninety percent chance of precipitation, bringing expected rainfall totals between a tenth and a quarter of an inch. There are no active weather alerts. Sunrise will be at seven twelve a.m., and sunset at six p.m.

In Hollywood and screenwriting news, Deadline reports that the CBS daytime drama Beyond the Gates triumphed at the fifty-third annual Daytime Emmy Awards with four major wins in its first year of eligibility, including trophies for Outstanding Lead Actor and Emerging Actress. The Hollywood Reporter notes that Margaret Qualley and Jack Antonoff have filed for divorce after three years of marriage. Meanwhile, Variety reports that Indian filmmaker Sanjay Gupta has died at the age of fifty-nine following a fatal fall at his Mumbai residence. In publishing news, Deadline reports that Angel Studios executive Jeff Harmon has laid out a strict new values-based content standard called The Angel Promise, which bans on-screen sex, nudity, the f-word, and the misuse of God's name across its distributed projects.

In artificial intelligence and technology, The Verge reports that major AI developers including OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic have agreed to back a new shared policy token standard proposed via the Internet Engineering Task Force. This new standard will allow publishers to apply website scraping preferences universally through robots.txt files instead of negotiating individually with every tech firm. TechCrunch notes that Google's first data center satellite has officially come online in space, running a Gemma four model on board its Tensor Processing Units and successfully transmitting its first AI-generated poetry back down to Earth.

Checking the weather in Rio de Janeiro, today brings light drizzle with a high near seventy-seven degrees and a low around seventy. Winds may gust up to twenty-four miles per hour, and the ultraviolet index reaches a very high level of nine. Sunrise was at five oh eight a.m., and sunset will arrive at six oh four p.m. local time.

Finally, in news from Brazil and Rio, G1 reports that local residents in Duque de Caxias experienced an intense shootout, which included a semi-truck being physically blocked across the Washington Luiz highway during ongoing security operations. Meanwhile, O Globo reports that Rio has kicked off its fourth annual Breakfast Weekend event, running through November twenty-ninth and featuring special breakfast menus at participating spots across the city.

That's the paper.

title: Friday, October 30
script:
Good morning. Today is Friday, October thirtieth, twenty twenty-six.

Starting off in Arkadelphia, expect mostly cloudy skies today with a high near seventy-nine degrees and calm winds drifting east-northeast up to five miles per hour. There is a zero percent chance of rain through the day. Tonight, the cloud cover stays firmly in place as temperatures settle to an overnight low around fifty-five degrees, with light northeast winds and an eight percent chance of precipitation. There are no active weather alerts across Clark County. The sun rose at seven thirty a.m. and will go down this evening at six twenty p.m.

Moving into the top national and world news, cryptocurrency exchange Binance has suspended transactions following what is suspected to be the largest cyber heist in history. The Wall Street Journal and the BBC report hackers compromised the platform in an attack totaling six point three billion dollars, prompting an immediate halt to trades as investigators trace the stolen funds. Overseas in Eastern Europe, Ukrainian forces launched a direct strike on a Russian oil refinery, bringing an end to a recent operational pause and directly defying warnings from President Trump. Out in Oregon, three people are dead after two helicopters collided in midair near McMinnville Airport on Thursday afternoon. Aviation authorities confirm an Airbus helicopter and a Robinson R twenty-two crashed into an open field adjacent to a highway, leaving no survivors. Back in Washington, the battle for the upcoming midterms is intensifying as more than forty-three million early ballots have already been cast, propelled by high turnout among Hispanic voters in key counties. The competitive landscape for control of the Senate continues to broaden in these final days, while national Democrats are spending heavily in state legislative races, attempting to chip away at the ten-state advantage held by Republicans. Meanwhile, an investigation by NPR revealed that more than fifteen thousand American military veterans were forced into significantly higher home loans, often paying an extra one thousand dollars every month, after a critical Veterans Affairs loan program was shut down during the Trump administration.

Turning to football, the Kansas City Chiefs are trying to recalibrate after suffering their first loss of the season, a brutal twenty to three defeat against the Seattle Seahawks. That outing generated historically low offensive numbers, with Patrick Mahomes throwing for just one hundred sixty-five yards on nineteen of thirty-three passing, averaging five yards per attempt with a passer rating of fifty-eight point three. Speaking on his New Heights podcast, tight end Travis Kelce was blunt, emphasizing that nobody in the locker room can be okay with being mediocre. Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo defended his group by stating that sack totals do not tell the full story, though pass rusher Chris Jones has recorded just half a sack and three quarterback hits through six games. On the injury report, rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane missed practice on Thursday due to a shoulder injury suffered while giving up a touchdown to Jaxon Smith-Njigba against Seattle. Special teams coordinator Dave Toub also addressed the recent signing of veteran kicker Justin Tucker to the practice squad, clarifying that the move is meant to push starter Harrison Butker rather than replace him. The Chiefs now turn their focus to a massive AFC West rematch this Sunday afternoon at three twenty-five p.m. against the Denver Broncos, where a win would give Kansas City a commanding three-game divisional lead. Around the league, Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson made an improbable return to the field on Thursday night after being transported to a hospital during the game, while the Seattle Seahawks prepare their dominant defense to face Chicago Bears rookie quarterback Caleb Williams and the league's top-ranked rushing attack.

Checking in on Jayhawks basketball, the Kansas men's team has officially been picked to finish third in the Big Twelve preseason media poll, mirroring their third-place finish in the conference coaches' poll. The Arizona Wildcats took top billing, followed closely by the Houston Cougars in second place. Kansas will be anchored this winter by five-star freshman forward Tyran Stokes, who captured another major preseason honor this week ahead of his collegiate debut. Fellow frontcourt contributor Keanu Dawes was also named to a national preseason watch list, giving head coach Bill Self plenty of talent to lean on as Kansas looks ahead to the twenty twenty-six, twenty twenty-seven college basketball campaign.

For fantasy football managers setting lineups for Week Eight, injuries and practice participation are forcing some critical decisions. Green Bay receiver Christian Watson provided immediate relief after returning to Thursday Night Football following an alarming hospital trip. In Las Vegas, tight end Brock Bowers received encouraging medical feedback ahead of Sunday's game against the New York Jets, significantly easing lineup worries. Jets running back Breece Hall also had his practice status clarified ahead of the trip west. Running back RJ Harvey was a surprise addition to Thursday's injury report, participating in a limited fashion with an undisclosed ailment. Philadelphia running back Kenneth Gainwell and Jadarian Price were also limited in Thursday workouts, while Seattle running back Zach Charbonnet logged a full session, solidifying his role for the weekend. Buccaneers wideout Emeka Egbuka landed on the injury report leading into a divisional clash with Atlanta, and managers are keeping a close watch on AJ Brown, whose knee and ankle issues threaten his availability. On the waiver wire, Carolina running back Jonathon Brooks and Washington's Jeremy McNichols are generating heavy trade and waiver interest as backfield touches shift across the league.

Shifting to the West Coast, Los Angeles is in for an overcast, damp Friday. Look for mostly cloudy skies with a high near seventy degrees and light south winds around five miles per hour. There is a fifty percent chance of rain throughout the day, though new precipitation totals are expected to remain under a tenth of an inch. Rain chances hold steady at fifty percent tonight under mostly cloudy skies, with overnight lows dipping to fifty-nine degrees and localized accumulations reaching up to a quarter of an inch. No active weather alerts are in effect across Los Angeles County. Sunrise was at seven eleven a.m., and the sun will set at six oh one p.m.

In entertainment news, members of SAG-AFTRA voted overwhelmingly to ratify the twenty twenty-six Television Animation Agreement and Basic Cable Animation Agreement, with nearly ninety-five percent casting approval ballots. The four-year agreement guarantees voice actors a twelve point six percent wage increase over its lifespan alongside strengthened protections regarding artificial intelligence. In television development, Matthew Weiner has departed Peacock's high-profile drama series The Chairman, which stars Eddie Murphy. Weiner had been attached as writer, executive producer, and showrunner, but Universal Television and One Hundred One Studios are now close to securing a replacement. On the technology front, AI dubbing startup Flawless, which spent one hundred million dollars developing SAG-AFTRA-endorsed voice software used on feature films like Fall, has sold off its core assets. An entity named TBellScout, backed by Dutch tech billionaire Steven Schuurman, purchased the company's TrueSync and DeepEditor intellectual property, leaving the broader future of Flawless uncertain. Across the studio landscape, Skydance is reorganizing international operations following its massive one hundred ten billion dollar merger, resulting in the exit of European and African chief Andrew Georgiou. And on the casting front, Poorna Jagannathan has joined Hulu's drama pilot Young Americans as a regular, with Natalia Leite set to direct.

Over in tech, Google has expanded Gemini by allowing users to generate, preview, and directly edit Google Docs, Sheets, slide presentations, Markdown files, and raw code right inside Gemini chat windows without leaving the workspace. In the startup world, Anthropic filed its S-One registration statement to go public on the Nasdaq, aiming for a valuation between one point five trillion and two trillion dollars while signaling to Wall Street that aggressive compute spending will continue unabated. Microsoft is simultaneously adjusting its operational footprint, offering voluntary buyouts to approximately sixty thousand employees across the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, and India as the company reallocates capital into artificial intelligence infrastructure. In open-source software, French startup Mistral released the model weights for a new trillion-parameter artificial intelligence model specifically engineered for enterprise cybersecurity defenses. Meanwhile, Amazon chief executive Andy Jassy told investors that Amazon Web Services is on track to become a one trillion dollar revenue business fueled by enterprise artificial intelligence demand, even as broader tech stocks wobbled on rising infrastructure capital expenditure.

Heading down to South America, Rio de Janeiro is dealing with widespread rain. Expect persistent showers today with a high near seventy-six degrees and an overnight low around seventy. The chance of rain sits at one hundred percent, accompanied by localized wind gusts reaching up to twenty-eight miles per hour. The UV index will reach six. The sun rose locally at five oh eight a.m. and will set this evening at six oh four p.m.

Finishing up with news from Brazil, Rio's municipal monitoring service Alerta Rio confirmed that this month has officially become the wettest October in twenty-nine years, dating back to when accurate citywide rain tracking began. The torrential conditions have contributed to severe transport problems across the region. On the Presidente Dutra highway, a commuter bus driver tragically died behind the wheel, sparking a catastrophic chain-reaction pileup involving at least twenty vehicles that completely shut down traffic heading toward the city of Rio. In the northern neighborhood of Vila Isabel, a massive tree collapsed across Boulevard Twenty-Eight of September, forcing municipal transit teams to close the major thoroughfare. On the political front, Washington Democrats are demanding formal answers from the State Department regarding former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro's arrival in the United States, even as sources close to Donald Trump indicate he has no intentions of endorsing Bolsonaro's claim to lead Brazil. In industrial news, Chinese automotive investors are reportedly preparing to accept state tax incentives to take over the shuttered Land Rover manufacturing facility in Rio de Janeiro state. Finally, the Rio Municipal Health Department reminds residents that adults up to fifty-nine years of age have until Saturday to receive their meningococcal ACWY vaccine at local clinics.

That's the paper.

title: Thursday, October 29
script:
Good morning. Today is Thursday, October twenty-ninth, twenty twenty-six.

In Arkadelphia, expect mostly sunny skies today with a high reaching near eighty-four degrees. Winds will remain calm out of the southeast at around zero miles per hour, with only a two percent chance of rain. Tonight brings mostly cloudy conditions and a low around fifty-one degrees, accompanied by an east-northeast wind around zero miles per hour and a one percent chance of precipitation. There are no active weather alerts. Sunrise was at seven twenty-nine a.m., and sunset will be at six twenty-one p.m.

Turning to national and international headlines.

Artificial intelligence is rapidly altering modern military operations, with both Russia and Ukraine deploying AI-powered drones that operate faster and with greater capability. Per NPR, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that automated systems could start directing battlefield decisions as early as next year. Meanwhile, train travel safety is under intense scrutiny in Europe following a tragic high-speed rail collision in Spain. In Toledo, south of Madrid, one high-speed train struck another stalled train from behind, raising the confirmed death toll to sixty-nine people among the more than five hundred passengers on board across the trains. Audio recordings released from the control center indicate that one driver received clearance to move despite the stalled train ahead.

In sports, history was made on the diamond as the Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Tampa Bay Rays to capture the first World Series title in franchise history. Playing in the smallest market in Major League Baseball, the victory arrives in the fifty-eighth season for the franchise, which originally began as the Seattle Pilots in nineteen sixty-nine. Back on the political front, NPR reports that both major parties are pouring heavy funding into competitive congressional districts ahead of the November third midterm elections. Advertising data reveals seventy House districts where Democrats and Republicans are each spending over six figures in the final stretch, including several traditional conservative strongholds.

Moving over to football and the National Football League.

The Kansas City Chiefs are picking up the pieces after a tough twenty to three loss to the Seattle Seahawks, dropping their record to five and one. Kansas City struggled heavily on third down throughout the contest, converting on just three of eleven attempts and failing to sustain offensive drives. There is some positive news on the injury front, as wide receiver Rashee Rice returned to practice as a limited participant after suffering a hamstring injury in week four. Right tackle Jaylon Moore also returned to full practice following his concussion protocol.

Off the field, the Chiefs made waves by signing veteran kicker Justin Tucker to their practice squad following recent kicking struggles from Harrison Butker, who missed two field goals last week. Head coach Andy Reid defended the move, noting that Tucker took care of his business during his workouts. Around the rest of the league, power rankings are shifting significantly heading into week eight. Per Arrowhead Pride, the Minnesota Vikings stand as the lone remaining undefeated team in the league at six and oh, while the Los Angeles Chargers remain the only winless team.

Shifting over to college basketball and college hoops.

The Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team is solidifying its rotation as head coach Bill Self evaluates lineup combinations following recent exhibition action. Coaches are weighing starting spots and playing time across a deep roster as official non-conference play approaches. On the recruiting and national awards front, incoming prospect Tyran Stokes continues to gather accolades, earning another spot on a major preseason watch list and securing strong positional rankings from ESPN analysts.

Turning to fantasy football updates for your roster.

Fantasy managers have a batch of key injury updates and roster moves to monitor ahead of week eight action. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is expected to play this week, giving a boost to standard lineup setups. In Green Bay, wide receiver Matthew Golden was upgraded on the official injury report, easing concerns for managers holding him in starting spots. Running back Jeremiyah Love of the Arizona Cardinals was limited in Wednesday's practice as the team monitors his workload.

On the transaction wire, the Houston Texans claimed running back Emari Demercado off waivers, offering potential depth in deeper leagues. Meanwhile, fantasy managers relying on Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown are keeping a close eye on his health, as his injury status remains one of the top headlines impacting week eight lineup decisions.

Taking a look now at the weather forecast for Los Angeles.

Los Angeles will see mostly cloudy conditions today with a high near seventy-four degrees and a gentle south wind reaching up to ten miles per hour. Rain chances remain low during the day at eight percent. Tonight, skies stay mostly cloudy with a low around sixty-two degrees and a twenty percent chance of light rain, primarily between eleven p.m. and five a.m., with potential rainfall totals staying under a tenth of an inch. There are no active weather alerts in effect. Sunrise was at seven ten a.m., and sunset is set for six oh two p.m.

Moving into news from Hollywood and the entertainment industry.

In entertainment production news, Abundantia Entertainment and video tech company InVideo have officially launched principal photography in Mumbai on Beta Builder. Deadline reports the project is the first hybrid artificial intelligence feature film from their strategic partnership, starring Mayur More and Ashlesha Thakur under the direction of Hridaye Nagpal. Meanwhile, international distribution networks are expanding their ties with Japanese intellectual property. Cannes Marché du Film and Tokyo's TIFFCOM announced they will host the second annual Japan IP Market in Cannes in May twenty twenty-seven, helping global producers secure adaptation rights for Japanese manga and books.

In executive insights from the Tokyo International Film Festival, Toho chief executive officer Matsuoka Hiro reflected on the massive domestic success of Godzilla Minus One. The film earned over eleven million dollars during its opening weekend in the United States, a result Matsuoka noted stemmed from taking an experimental distribution gamble rather than executing a long-term strategic plan. On television, South Park targeted Grand Theft Auto VI anticipation in its latest episode on Comedy Central, poking fun at food inflation, tariffs, and gaming hype while incorporating parody gameplay elements.

Turning to artificial intelligence and technology updates.

Google has announced the release of Gemini four Carbon, its newest frontier artificial intelligence model. According to company benchmark reports, Carbon claimed the top spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index ahead of competing models Claude Opus five point five and GPT six Astra. Gemini four Carbon delivers substantial improvements in software coding, automated agent tasks, and cybersecurity defense, though access is currently restricted to select cybersecurity defense partners through Google's Fairwind Program.

In corporate earnings, Microsoft disclosed record financial performance for the tenth consecutive quarter, generating ninety-two point three billion dollars in quarterly revenue, up nineteen percent year over year. For the first time, Microsoft publicly broke out revenue figures for Azure, revealing thirty-three point two billion dollars in quarterly revenue, alongside ten billion dollars generated from its commercial partnership with OpenAI. Elsewhere in software updates, Google expanded Chrome's enhanced autofill feature. Powered by Gemini with Personal Intelligence, the browser can now securely search a user's Gmail inbox with permission to automatically populate form fields with flight details, shipping numbers, and order confirmations.

Finally, Meta indicated it will likely delay the rollout of its controversial new business terms past November twentieth. The decision follows widespread opposition from news publishers who raised legal and financial concerns over terms that allowed Meta to train AI models on publisher web content.

Checking in on the weather forecast for Rio de Janeiro.

Rio de Janeiro is experiencing light rain today with temperatures reaching a high near seventy-four degrees Fahrenheit and dropping to a low around sixty-nine. Precipitation is guaranteed today with a one hundred percent chance of rain, accompanied by wind gusts reaching up to fourteen miles per hour and a moderate UV index of five. Local sunrise was at five oh nine a.m., and sunset will occur at six oh three p.m. local time.

Concluding today with national and regional news from Brazil.

Following his recent electoral defeat in Brazil, Flávio Bolsonaro fled the country and arrived in Florida after receiving family visas from the Trump administration. Brazilian judicial authorities had issued an order to seize his passport as part of an expanding federal investigation into illegal gambling, money laundering, and financial concealment. Upon landing in Miami, Bolsonaro publicly claimed to be the rightful leader of Brazil, creating fresh diplomatic strain.

In Rio de Janeiro, Brazil's Federal Police executed a new phase of Operation Unha e Carne, targeting a sophisticated money laundering ring that hid assets through real estate, private aircraft, and luxury automobiles. Federal investigators are probing formal connections between organized crime groups and local politicians across the state. In local law enforcement actions, police in Rio arrested the leader of a home invasion gang that targeted luxury residences in Niterói, including the home of a local city councilor, while military police detained a man and a teenager seized with illegal firearms and narcotics in Gardênia Azul.

That's the paper.

title: Wednesday, October 28
script:
Good morning. Today is Wednesday, October 28, 2026.

Starting in Arkadelphia, you are looking at a clear night with an overnight low around forty-six degrees and calm winds. Wednesday brings wall-to-wall sunshine with a high near eighty-four degrees and winds staying near zero. Wednesday night stays mostly clear with a low around forty-nine and light east-northeast winds. Rain chances hover between one and two percent through the period, and there are no active weather alerts. Sunrise is at seven twenty-eight a.m. and sunset is at six twenty-two p.m.

In top headlines, a high-speed train slammed into the rear of a stopped train in central Spain on Wednesday, derailing two cars and killing at least ten people according to local authorities. In the Middle East, partial results from a contentious election in Israel show no clear winner, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc running neck-and-neck with opposition rival Gadi Eisenkot and both falling short of a majority without relying on Arab parties. Meanwhile, luxury cruise passengers on the Villa Vie Odyssey have been left stranded in Cambodia due to soaring fuel costs, forcing the ship to suspend its voyage and work with passengers on temporary living arrangements. In U.S. politics, a new report from Fwd.us reveals that the number of local and state police officers working directly with Immigration and Customs Enforcement has doubled over the past eight months. Additionally, congressional Democrats are partnering with governance groups to build action plans against potential election fraud claims, while the number of out-of-state donations flooding competitive U.S. Senate races continues to surge.

Shifting to football, the Kansas City Chiefs are picking up the pieces after a humbling twenty to three loss to the Seattle Seahawks in primetime. The defeat exposed real problems for Kansas City, particularly a stagnant offense that failed to reach the red zone and a defense that struggled to get off the field. Rumors are swirling that the front office is calling around about potential wide receiver trades ahead of the deadline to bolster an offense missing the injured Tyquan Thornton, while kicker Harrison Butker faces potential roster competition following recent struggles. Elsewhere in the NFL, a dramatic turnaround by the Minnesota Vikings and a late collapse by the Los Angeles Chargers combined for a first-of-its-kind statistical anomaly in the league.

In Kansas basketball, the Duke Blue Devils recently raced past the Kansas Jayhawks in a matchup that highlighted early-season roster moves under coach Jon Scheyer. On the wider collegiate front, NCAA officials named Kansas City among the finalist cities to host future men's and women's Final Fours between twenty thirty-two and twenty thirty-six.

For fantasy football managers navigating week eight, must-add waiver wire pickups worth grabbing include wide receiver Alec Pierce and running back Austin Ekeler alongside running backs Jonah Coleman and Rachaad White. On the injury front, Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is expected to play against the Buffalo Bills, while fantasy managers continue tracking the recovery timelines of players like James Conner, Tyler Warren, DJ Moore, and Rashee Rice.

Out west, Los Angeles weather starts with patchy fog before eleven a.m. followed by mostly cloudy skies and a high near seventy-six degrees. South-southeast winds will stay light between zero and five miles per hour with a zero percent chance of rain. Wednesday night brings more mostly cloudy skies, an overnight low of fifty-eight degrees, and a slight three percent chance of rain, with no active weather alerts. Sunrise hits at seven oh nine a.m. and sunset is at six oh three p.m.

In Hollywood and screenwriting news, Russell Brand took the stand at Southwark Crown Court for his criminal rape trial, forcefully denying all charges against him and testifying that his entire life has been consumed by the allegations while noting no one agreed to testify on his behalf. At the Tokyo International Film Festival market, Amazon MGM Studios Japan announced it is doubling its investment in original content to meet global standards, while Academy CEO Bill Kramer noted that international membership has surged from five percent to twenty-five percent over the last decade. Meanwhile, a new Interbrand report revealed that the entertainment sector has overtaken the automotive industry to become the world's second most valuable business sector, with cumulative brand values hitting three hundred thirty-two billion five hundred million dollars.

In AI and technology, Google announced its Genie four world model, which generates interactive simulations with improved physics, added audio, and real-time natural language steering for up to two minutes. Apple is bringing an AI assistant built on models from Apple and OpenAI to its productivity suite—including Pages, Keynote, and Numbers—to help users draft text, design slides, and analyze data. Meanwhile, Mozilla is updating its browser's Smart Window feature to let users automatically fill out online forms by pulling relevant information directly from open browser tabs.

Heading south to Rio de Janeiro, today brings overcast skies with a high near seventy-seven degrees and an overnight low of sixty-six. Expect wind gusts up to thirty-two miles per hour, a UV index of eight, and a zero percent chance of rain. Sunrise is at five ten a.m. and sunset is at six oh two p.m., local time.

In Brazilian national and local news, Flávio Bolsonaro fled the country via Argentina and landed in Miami following an election defeat, despite previously claiming he would hand over his passports and never leave Brazil. In the financial sector, Brazil’s largest lender has become the first bank to formalize a crypto brokerage under newly updated regulatory rules. Locally in Rio de Janeiro, police launched a major operation targeting a gas-selling monopoly tied to the Comando Vermelho criminal group that forced local businesses and residents to pay up to one hundred fifty reals per cooking gas cylinder. A separate police sweep targeted the sexual exploitation of adolescents, while labor prosecutors have asked a court to condemn state lawmaker India Armelau for electoral harassment after she allegedly encouraged business owners to fire workers who voted for the Workers' Party.

That's the paper.

title: Tuesday, October 27
script:
Good morning, today is Tuesday, October twenty-seventh, twenty twenty-six.

Starting in Arkadelphia, expect a partly sunny day with a high near seventy-nine degrees and a low tonight around forty-six. Winds will be calm with a zero to three percent chance of rain, and no active weather alerts. Sunrise is at seven twenty-seven a.m. and sunset will be at six twenty-three p.m.

In top news, a new NPR, PBS News, and Marist poll shows Democrats hold significant advantages going into Election Day, though lagging enthusiasm among key groups suggests gains may not come easy. Meanwhile, President Trump campaigned in Monday in Mississippi, where the U.S. Senate race has seen millions in last-minute spending as Republicans face stiff challenges in a state with the largest proportional Black population in the country. In prediction markets, Polymarket has hired a former FBI official to investigate dozens of cases to ensure political insiders do not profit from confidential election information. In international news, a localized ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia took effect early Tuesday in Oleshky, brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump to allow aid deliveries and civilian evacuations, even as missile attacks resumed in Kyiv. Voters in Israel have also headed to the polls for a pivotal election defined by security and democracy, with many fearing neither leading political bloc will win a majority, which could lead to weeks or months of political wrangling. In sports and culture, Harry Kane has won the Ballon d'Or, becoming the first Englishman to take the trophy in twenty-five years, while Kylian Mbappé was dropped by major Chinese brands following backlash over a social media joke. Additionally, Jay-Z announced he will headline the Super Bowl halftime show on February fourteenth at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

Turning to the NFL, the Kansas City Chiefs fell to five and one after a twenty-to-three blowout loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday night. The Chiefs' offense had a historically poor showing, failing to reach the red zone or the end zone all evening, while tight end Travis Kelce moved into the top five all-time in career receptions despite the defeat. The team is now looking ahead to a crucial game against the Denver Broncos as questions swirl around the offensive line and wide receiver play. Elsewhere in the league, the Milwaukee Brewers routed the Tampa Bay Rays ten to one to move within one victory of their first World Series title, led by twenty-two-year-old Jackson Chourio's four-hit postseason performance.

In Kansas basketball news, the Jayhawks concluded their exhibition slate with a ninety to eighty-four loss to Duke inside Allen Fieldhouse, marking their second straight preseason defeat following a hard-fought loss to Louisville. Head coach Bill Self's squad utilized small ball lineups against the Blue Devils, and the team now turns its full attention to the upcoming regular season competition.

For fantasy football, Week eight waiver wire targets feature players like Jonah Cooper Junior and Jonah Coleman, while managers monitoring the injury report will be tracking updates on Christian McCaffrey, Saquon Barkley, and Lamar Jackson following Monday night action.

Moving to Los Angeles, it will be sunny with a high near seventy-seven degrees and a low tonight around fifty-seven with patchy fog after eleven p.m. Winds will be light out of the south southeast with a one percent chance of rain and no active alerts. Sunrise is at seven oh eight a.m. and sunset at six oh four p.m.

In Hollywood, Jay-Z has officially been confirmed to headline the Apple Music Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show in twenty twenty-seven at SoFi Stadium. In publishing and television news, Noah Wyle has been named People's Sexiest Man Alive for the first time, and Taylor Swift was inducted into the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame as its youngest member at thirty-six. Additionally, Lionsgate's horror-comedy Ghosts: The Possession of Button House claimed the top spot at the U.K. and Ireland box office with two million four hundred thousand pounds in its opening weekend, and Neil Young filed a ten million dollar lawsuit against Donald Trump for using Rockin' in the Free World at campaign events.

In AI and tech, Anthropic has officially filed its S-1 prospectus with the SEC for an initial public offering on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT, revealing soaring revenue alongside mounting data center natural gas dependencies and enterprise growth. Meanwhile, OpenAI has launched GPT-6.1 Terra, a faster and cheaper model focused on app control and everyday work, and Microsoft has offered voluntary buyouts to up to sixty thousand employees across the U.S., U.K., Canada, and India to trim staff without another round of layoffs.

Down in Rio de Janeiro, expect light drizzle today with a high near seventy-three degrees and a low around sixty-six. Winds will gust up to twenty-three miles per hour with a twenty-nine percent chance of rain and a high UV index of eight. Sunrise is at five ten a.m. and sunset at six oh two p.m. local time.

In Brazilian news, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's presidential runoff victory has put the brakes on the rise of the far right in Latin America, though the win immediately impacted markets with state-controlled oil firm Petrobras shedding twenty-four billion dollars in value in a single session. In local Rio news, the iconic Sugarloaf Mountain cable car is celebrating its one hundred and fourteenth anniversary with special programming, and police at Galeão Airport seized more than eight kilograms of cocaine hidden in a suitcase structure.

That's the paper.

title: Monday, October 26
script:
Good morning. Today is Monday, October 26, 2026.

Starting off in Arkadelphia, Arkansas, you can expect partly sunny skies today with a high near seventy-eight degrees. Winds will be calm out of the east at around zero miles per hour, and there is a zero percent chance of rain. Tonight brings mostly cloudy conditions with a low dropping down to around forty-six degrees and light east-northeast winds. There are no active weather alerts in effect for the area. Sunrise was at seven twenty-six a.m., and sunset will be at six twenty-four p.m.

Moving to world and national headlines, eighty-year-old left-wing leader Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a fourth term as president of Brazil after defeating Flávio Bolsonaro in a fiercely contested runoff election. Flávio Bolsonaro has so far refused to recognize the defeat, creating political tension across the country as global leaders react to the shift.

In Serbia, long-time populist leader Aleksandar Vučić lost power to a student-led protest movement, marking the end of his twelve-year reign in an election billed as a referendum on the nation's future. Meanwhile, Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado made a high-profile return to crowds in Venezuela after spending more than ten months in exile following an escape by speedboat.

On the domestic political front, President Trump escalated attacks against Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed on Sunday, framing him as a national security threat and questioning his loyalty to the United States. Rapper Nicki Minaj joined Trump on stage at a Michigan rally as Republicans fight tight races in redrawn congressional districts that were expected to be safer seats. Trump also lashed out at talk show host Bill Maher in a long social media post, calling him a complete loser just nine days after dining with him at the White House.

In public health news, United States officials report that national measles cases have more than doubled compared to last year. Pennsylvania has been hit hardest, confirming over one thousand three hundred thirty-eight cases across forty-four counties so far this year.

Finally, the entertainment world is mourning the loss of Emmy-winning voice actor Eric Bauza, who voiced iconic characters including Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, and recently starred in the film Coyote versus Acme. He passed away at forty-six years old.

Turning to football, the Kansas City Chiefs suffered their first loss of the season on Sunday Night Football, falling twenty to three against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. The Chiefs dropped to five and one on the year after being held to just two hundred ten total yards and converting only three of ten third downs. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes struggled behind backup offensive tackles, while kicker Harrison Butker missed a fifty-eight yard field goal before halftime, prompting head coach Andy Reid to admit his kicker is off a bit. Linebacker Nick Bolton briefly left the game with an injury, but Reid reported no major long-term injuries after the final whistle. Off the field, pregame reports revealed left tackle Josh Simmons was asked to leave a team meeting earlier in the week by Reid and Mahomes after sitting with his feet up. Looking ahead, Kansas City opens as a one and a half point favorite for their Week Eight divisional matchup against the Denver Broncos at Mile High Stadium.

On the hardwood, the Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team dropped a high-profile preseason exhibition game to Duke on Sunday, falling ninety to eighty-four in the Blue Blood Classic. Despite the loss in a game that does not count toward the official record, the Jayhawks used the national television showcase to test their lineup ahead of the regular season opener.

In fantasy football news, managers should monitor the situation in Seattle after wide receiver Rashid Shaheed suffered an injury early in the third quarter against Kansas City and was ruled out for the remainder of the game alongside teammate Velus Jones Jr. Elsewhere around the league, Cincinnati wide receiver Tee Higgins put up a huge performance in Week Seven, boosting his stock back into high-end starter territory. Heading into Week Eight waiver wires, managers should look for potential additions like Jakobi Meyers or James Conner if available, while evaluating underperforming roster spots to make room for midseason surges.

Over in Los Angeles, expect sunny skies today with a high near seventy-seven degrees and light west-northwest winds around five to ten miles per hour. Tonight will be mostly clear with a low around fifty-seven degrees and a gentle southeast wind. The chance of precipitation remains at zero percent, and there are no active weather alerts for the region. Sunrise was at seven zero seven a.m., and sunset will be at six zero five p.m.

In entertainment news, Disney Plus has picked up international streaming rights for the RTÉ and BBC drama series The Walsh Sisters. Based on Marian Keyes' bestselling books, the show was the highest-rated drama on Irish television over the last two years and has already been renewed for a second season.

DC Studios co-head James Gunn addressed online criticism regarding the continuity of his upcoming slate, defending the connected storylines across film and television projects against comparisons to Marvel.

In executive news, Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos traveled to Seoul to celebrate the ten-year anniversary of the streaming service operating in South Korea, highlighting global hits like Squid Game and upcoming Korean originals.

On the sales market, Epsilon Film acquired global distribution rights for the animated family feature Apple Cadabra - I Shrunk Myself ahead of the upcoming American Film Market in Los Angeles.

In technology news, xAI's Grok released the first seven minutes of its AI-generated video project titled Odyssey, giving viewers an early look at its text-to-video capabilities.

A new report from an Apollo economist revealed that despite massive corporate spending and industry excitement surrounding artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech companies.

In the open-source community, moderators of the popular open-source subreddit banned all projects that use, are generated by, or target artificial intelligence, stating that current AI tools run counter to open-source philosophy.

Retail giant Gap Incorporated announced it is scaling Bridgette, an artificial intelligence tool designed to streamline seasonal hiring across its retail stores and distribution hubs.

Taking a look at weather in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, heavy drizzle is expected throughout the day with a high near seventy-two degrees Fahrenheit and a low around sixty-six degrees. Rain probability is at one hundred percent with strong wind gusts up to forty-one miles per hour and a low UV index of two. Sunrise local time was at five eleven a.m., and sunset will occur at six zero one p.m.

Finishing in Brazil, political turmoil continues following President Lula's narrow victory over Flávio Bolsonaro. Flávio Bolsonaro's refusal to concede has rattled local markets, while financial analysts monitor rising odds that Brazil's central bank will hold interest rates steady. The federal government is also allowing a major diesel subsidy worth about forty-two cents a liter to lapse today without an extension, even as international crude oil prices remain elevated.

In local Rio de Janeiro news, election results show President Lula won inside the city of Rio with fifty-one point five four percent of the valid vote. However, Flávio Bolsonaro captured majorities in neighboring municipalities including Maricá, Saquarema, and São Pedro da Aldeia.

Tragedy struck the metropolitan region as a fourteen-year-old teenager died following a building collapse in São João de Meriti.

Looking ahead to the local economy, Rio de Janeiro is preparing for the upcoming cruise season starting Thursday, which is projected to bring a thirty-three percent increase in port calls and generate roughly two hundred forty-six million reais in revenue.

That's the paper.

title: Sunday, October 25
script:
Good morning. Today is Sunday, October twenty-fifth, twenty twenty-six.

Starting off in Arkadelphia, you can expect a calm, sunny autumn day. The high will reach near eighty degrees with light east winds between zero and five miles per hour, following an overnight low of forty-four. Tonight, expect mostly cloudy skies as the temperature drops back down to around forty-seven degrees with calm northeast winds. There is zero chance of rain on the board, and no active weather alerts are in effect. The sun rose at seven twenty-six this morning and will set at six twenty-five this evening.

Turning to the top headlines from around the world, mass demonstrations swept across several European nations on Saturday. BBC News reports that nearly one thousand people were arrested following clashes during massive protests across France. Demonstrations also spread to Rome, Madrid, Lisbon, Tirana, and Milan, where soldiers were deployed to guard the city center as thousands marched through the streets.

In Ukraine, satellite internet access is stabilizing following extended outages. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed that standard Starlink connection speeds have been restored after more than a week of severe disruptions. Elon Musk subsequently stated that SpaceX had deliberately restricted Ukraine's Starlink connection speeds, alleging that the country violated the platform's terms of service by using the satellite network for military operations.

Here at home, the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of New York has reached an eight hundred million dollar settlement to resolve claims of sexual abuse. According to plaintiff counsel, all thirteen hundred survivors of abuse committed by clergy and lay workers have agreed to the terms of the landmark agreement.

On the national political front, campaign activity is intensifying ahead of the midterm elections. NPR reports that Republicans have spent millions of dollars playing defense in conservative Arkansas, while Democrats are watching independent candidates in Nebraska and Montana to see if they can help flip Senate control. Meanwhile, former President Barack Obama hit the campaign trail for Democrats this weekend, sharply criticizing the Trump administration's policies and framing the upcoming vote as a critical check on executive power.

Out on the field, the Kansas City Chiefs are in the Pacific Northwest tonight to take on the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday Night Football. A major storyline centers on running back Kenneth Walker, who returns to Seattle for the first time since leaving in free agency. Walker signed a three-year contract worth over fourteen million dollars annually with Kansas City after earning Super Bowl MVP honors with the Seahawks in February, and he currently leads the league in rushing. Before departing for Seattle, the Chiefs made several roster adjustments on Saturday. Kansas City signed running back Jaydn Ott from the practice squad to an active contract, activated linebacker Cooper McDonald from injured reserve, and elevated wide receiver Justin Watson from the practice squad. To make room, the Chiefs placed running back Brashard Smith on injured reserve. Cornerback L'Jarius Sneed traveled separately to Seattle ahead of tonight's kickoff.

Across the wider league, several key injuries are altering Week Seven lineups. Per NBC Sports, wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks have both been ruled out for today's contests, while running back Jonah Coleman makes his return from injury. Receiver Puka Nacua enters the weekend listed as questionable, leaving offenses shuffling options across the board.

For Jayhawks basketball fans, preseason preparation is front and center as Kansas gears up for men's hoops action. The team is preparing for a high-profile exhibition matchup against Duke as the squad finalizes its early rotations before the regular season begins.

If you are setting your fantasy football lineups this morning, injuries are forcing plenty of last-minute adjustments. With DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks sidelined and Puka Nacua questionable, fantasy managers need backup plans ready at wide receiver. In Seattle, the absence of running back Zach Charbonnet clears additional room in the backfield against Kansas City, while managers are also tracking late evaluations on Saquon Barkley, Breece Hall, and Jordan Mason. If you need immediate help off the waiver wire, RotoBaller highlights wide receiver Caleb Douglas as an emerging pickup for Week Seven, alongside Dylan Sampson and Ted Hurst the Third. Additionally, FlurrySports points to Chicago receiver Rome Odunze as an appealing buy-low trade candidate for rosters looking to capitalize on shifting volume in the second half of the season.

Heading over to the West Coast, Los Angeles is in for another dry and pleasant day. The city will see full sunshine today with a high near seventy-seven degrees and light southeast winds between five and ten miles per hour. That follows a clear overnight low of fifty-seven. Tonight, expect partly cloudy skies with the mercury dipping back down to around fifty-seven degrees alongside light north winds. Rain chances remain at zero percent, and there are no active weather advisories. Sunrise was at seven oh six a.m., and the sun will set at six oh six p.m.

In entertainment news, the SAG-AFTRA National Board has voted overwhelmingly to secure its leadership for the long haul. The board approved an extension for National Executive Director Duncan Crabtree-Ireland through June twentieth, twenty thirty-two, with ninety-eight point three four percent voting in favor. The agreement also officially adds Chief Executive Officer to his title, extending his previous deal beyond its original twenty twenty-eight expiration date.

On the development side, Hulu is moving forward with an adaptation of Sarah MacLean's twenty twenty-five novel "These Summer Storms." The drama series is in development through Twentieth Television with Melanie Marnich writing and executive producing alongside Erin and Sara Foster through their production banner. The Foster sisters are also celebrating the release of the third season of their Netflix romantic comedy "Nobody Wants This," with Erin Foster noting she has plenty more story mapped out for a potential fourth season. Over at CBS Studios, Jessica Biel is executive producing a modernized reboot of the family drama "7th Heaven" through her Iron Ocean banner, aiming to bring the classic property to a new generation while fostering a safe and contemporary environment on set. In the legal space, artificial intelligence startup Anthropic is facing a major new lawsuit from music publishers, alleging the company infringed upon two hundred seventy-four Elvis Presley songs to train its AI models.

Looking closer at artificial intelligence and technology, new consumer tools and regulatory boundaries are taking shape. Financial tech firm Block has unveiled a new voice AI model called Dessa, which was trained entirely on human speech rather than text transcripts in order to capture natural emotional inflections. Block demonstrated that the model is efficient enough to run locally on a MacBook equipped with an M four Max processor.

On the state policy level, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro has signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act into law. The measure makes Pennsylvania one of the first states in the country to mandate clear disclosure labels on any advertising that has been significantly generated or modified by AI, covering television commercials, radio, text, and print flyers. Meanwhile, researchers are highlighting significant political polarization embedded in modern language models. A new study found that when forced to make a selection, Elon Musk's Grok model overwhelmingly favored Republican candidates while OpenAI's GPT favored Democrats, with the two models disagreeing in over ninety percent of nearly five hundred electoral races analyzed.

Traveling down to South America, Rio de Janeiro is dealing with heavy weather today. The city will see persistent, heavy showers with a high near seventy-five degrees and a low dipping to seventy-one. Rain chances sit at one hundred percent throughout the day, accompanied by wind gusts reaching up to thirty-two miles per hour and a minimal UV index of one. Sunrise was at five twelve a.m. local time, and sunset is scheduled for six oh one p.m.

Finally, in Brazil, millions of citizens are at the ballot box today for the second round of the country's presidential election. Incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, seeking a historic fourth term at eighty years old, faces a tight runoff challenge from conservative Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of the imprisoned former president. Flavio Bolsonaro officially cast his vote in Rio de Janeiro this morning after concluding his campaign on Saturday with a large rally at Praca do O in the city's Barra da Tijuca neighborhood. The two candidates have put forward sharply contrasting visions for Rio de Janeiro, with debates focusing on economic recovery, local security, and federal resource distribution.

In national economic and industry developments, Brazilian airline Azul has secured a federal credit-backed loan package of up to three hundred ninety-seven million dollars. The funds are earmarked exclusively for purchasing domestic jet fuel, designed to help the carrier navigate stubbornly high operating expenses that have slowed its post-restructuring financial recovery. On the agricultural front, neighboring Uruguay has enacted an indefinite suspension on imports and transit of all Brazilian poultry products after an outbreak of Newcastle disease was detected on a commercial turkey farm in the southern state of Santa Catarina. Back in Rio's metropolitan area, municipal planners announced that major macrodrainage flood control infrastructure works at the Caio Martins complex in Niteroi are now projected for completion in twenty twenty-nine.

That's the paper.
